questions.question: In the periodic table, the highly electronegative halogens and the highly electropositive alkali metals are separated by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Noble gases__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Highly negative halogens require only one electron to complete their octet
 
• Noble gases are those whose octet is complicated.
 
• Alkali metal has only one extra electron in its outermost element they want to lose it to complete octet
 
• Hence, halogen and alkali metals are separated by noble gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• In the periodic table of elements, there are seven horizontal rows of elements called periods. The vertical columns of elements are called groups, or families.
 
• The** Rare Earth Elements** make up the **middle block** of the periodic table.
 
• The **Rare Earth Elements** or transition metals occupy the short columns in the centre of the periodic table, between Group 2A and Group 3A. 
 
• They are sometimes called the *d*-block elements, since in this region the *d*-orbitals are being filled in, and are also referred to as B-group elements since in most numbering systems of the columns on the periodic table the numerals of these groups are followed by the letter B.

questions.question: The Periodic Law as we know it today owes its development to:

__
 
• **The Periodic Law, as we know it today owes its development to the Russian chemist, Dmitri Mendeleev (1834-1907) and the German chemist, Lothar Meyer (1830-1895).**
 
• Working independently, both the chemists in **1869** proposed that on arranging elements in the increasing order of their atomic weights, similarities appear in physical and chemical properties at regular intervals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Modern Periodic Table:**
 
• The Modern Periodic Table is classified into the following elements - **p-block, s-block, d-block, and f-block**.
 
• The** p-block** elements include **chalcogens, pnictogens, halogens, inert gases**.
 
 
• The** 18****th**** group** is known as Inert gas, zero groups, Nonreactive gases.
 
• The** 17****th**** group **is known as **Halogen**.
 
• The **16****th**** group** is known as **Chalcogen**.
 
• The **15****th**** group** is known as **Pnictogen**.
 
 
 
• The **s-block** elements include **alkali metals and alkaline earth metals**. 
 
• The **d-block** elements include **Transition elements**.
 
• The **f-block** elements include **Inner Transition Elements**.

questions.question: Which one of the following pair is an example of Isobars?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Calcium and argon are examples of a pair of Isobars**__. Calcium and argon have a mass number of 40. The atomic number of argon 18 and an atomic number of calcium is 20.
 
• Isobars:
 __
 
• These are atoms of the elements having the **same mass number but different atomic numbers**.
 
• They differ in the chemical property but has the same physical property.
 
• Example: argon, potassium and calcium.
 
 
 
• The mass number is the sum of a number of protons and neutrons in an atom of the elements is called the mass number.
 
 
• It is denoted by A.
 
 
 
• The atomic number is the number of proton or electrons in an atom of the element is called the atomic number.
 
 
• It is denoted by Z.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Isotopes: These are atoms of the elements having the same atomic number but a different mass number.

 
 
• The isotopes of hydrogen are Protium, Deuterium and Tritium
 
 
 
• Isotones: These are atoms of different elements having the same number of neutrons.
 
• Isoelectronic: These are atoms/molecules/ ions containing the same number of electrons.

questions.question: Identify the word that means vertical columns of Periodic Table.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Groups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The vertical columns of Periodic Table is called **Groups**.
 
• In chemistry, a group is a **column** of elements in the periodic table of the chemical elements.
 
• There are **18** numbered groups in the periodic table; the f-block columns (between groups 2 and 3) are not numbered.
 
• The elements in a **group** have similar physical or chemical characteristics of the outermost electron shells of their atoms (i.e., the same core charge), because most chemical properties are dominated by the orbital location of the outermost electron.
 
• Groups may also be identified using their **topmost element**, or have a specific name.
 
• For example, group 16 is also described as the "**oxygen group**" and as the "**chalcogens**".
 
• An exception is the "**iron group**", which usually refers to "**group 8**", but in chemistry may also mean iron, cobalt, and nickel, or some other set of elements with similar chemical properties.
 
• In astrophysics and nuclear physics, it usually refers to iron, cobalt, nickel, chromium, and manganese.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In chemistry and physics, a **valence electron** is an electron in the outer shell associated with an atom, and that can participate in the formation of a chemical bond if the outer shell is not closed.
 
• A **period** in the periodic table is a row of chemical elements. All elements in a row have the same number of electron shells. 
 
• The k, l, m, and n are called atomic **orbitals**. Filling up these orbitals with electrons builds atoms, and the way in which atoms are built up gives rise to the periodic table.

questions.question: Where is sodium located on the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**On the left side**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sodium is located on the **left side of the periodic table in the first group**.
 
• Sodium, atomic symbol** Na**, has an atomic number of** eleven, **and lies in** group 1 on the periodic table, **below** lithium **and to the** left of magnesium. **
 
• This element is in the **alkali metals family**, and it has only** one valence electron**.
 
• Sodium is** used as a heat exchanger** in some** nuclear reactors, **and as a **reagent** in the chemicals industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The periodic table is a tabular array of the chemical elements organized by atomic number, from the element with the lowest atomic number, hydrogen, to the element with the highest atomic number.
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** is the father of the periodic table.
 
• The **Modern Periodic Table **that we use was developed by **Henry Moseley**.
 
• In a periodic table elements are arranged in **columns, known as groups, and rows, called periods.**
 
• There are a total of 4 blocks in the periodic table named **s,p,d,f.**
 
• **S block** contains groups **1 (alkali metals) and 2 (alkaline earth metals**) elements.
 
• **P block **elements are found in periodic table groups **(13-18).**
 
• **D block** contains elements from groups **(3 to 12)**.
 
• **F block** contains **14 elements named Lanthanoides after (Lanthanum) La (57) and 14 elements called Actinoides after (Actinium) Ac (89).**

questions.question: Which group is on the second column from the right in the periodic table and contains fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I), astatine (At) and tennessine (Ts)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 17.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **group 17 elements include fluorine(F), chlorine(Cl), bromine(Br), iodine(I) and astatine(At)** from the top to the bottom.
 
• They are called “halogens” because they give salts when they react with metals.
 
• The elements in this group are all non-metals.
 
• The term 'halogen' is a Greek word which means 'salt former' because they react with metals to form compounds called salts**. For example, fluorine reacts explosively with sodium to form sodium fluoride. Hence group 17 are called halogens.**
 
• **Group 17 elements are called halogens**. The name halogens are from Greek halo (sea salt) and gens (producing formation) and thus means 'sea salt former'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A boron group element, any of the six chemical elements constituting Group 13 (IIIa) of the periodic table.
 
• **Groups 13–16 **of the periodic table contain one or more metalloids, in addition to metals, nonmetals, or both.
 
• Group 13 is called the boron group, and boron is the only metalloid in this group. The other group 13 elements are metals.
 
• Group 15 elements are also called the Nitrogen family. It includes n**itrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony and bismuth** elements.
 
• The** p-block** elements are also known as the Representative Elements which are placed on the right side of the main periodic table.
 
• The oxygen family, also called the chalcogens, consists of the elements found in Group 16 of the periodic table and is considered among the main group elements

questions.question: Who arranged the elements with chemically similar properties, such as lithium, sodium, and potassium, and showed that the properties of the middle element could be predicted from the properties of the other two?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Johann Dobereiner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Dobereiner **stated in his **law of triads **that **the arithmetic means of the atomic masses **of the **first and third element **in **a triad **would be **approximately equal **to **the atomic mass **of the **second element **in **that triad**.
 
• Also, when **elements are arranged **in **order of increasing atomic masses**, **groups of three elements(triads**), having **similar chemical properties **are obtained.
 
• The main **Limitation of Dobereiner's classification **of **elements was **that he **failed to arrange **all the **then-known elements in the form of triads **of elements having **similar chemical properties**.

• Halogens include five elements: **Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), Iodine (I), and Astatine (At)**.
 
• These elements are highly reactive nonmetals and are known for forming **salts** when they react with metals.
 
• Halogens have seven valence electrons, making them one electron short of a stable octet configuration, which accounts for their high reactivity.
 
• The chemical reactivity of halogens decreases down the group: **Fluorine > Chlorine > Bromine > Iodine > Astatine**.

• **Applications:**
 
 
• Fluorine is used in toothpaste (as fluoride) and Teflon production.
 
• Chlorine is used as a disinfectant and in the production of PVC (polyvinyl chloride).
 
• Bromine is used in flame retardants, while Iodine is vital for thyroid health.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity with Hydrogen:**
 
 
• Halogens react with hydrogen to form hydrogen halides (e.g., HF, HCl), which dissolve in water to form strong acids.
 
 
 
• **Occurrence:**
 
 
• Halogens are not found in their elemental state in nature due to their high reactivity but occur as halide ions in various compounds.
 
 
 
• **Trends in Group 17:**
 
 
• Electronegativity decreases down the group, with Fluorine being the most electronegative element in the periodic table.
 
• Oxidizing power decreases from Fluorine to Iodine.

questions.question: The general name of the elements of **"Group 17"** is ______.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

__
 
• A periodic table is an arrangement of elements based on their atomic numbers and chemical properties.
 
• It is divided into 18 groups and 7 periods running vertically and horizontally respectively.
 
• The periodic table accommodates a discrete combination of metal, non-metals, and metalloids.
 
• The elements in the periodic table are arranged horizontally in ascending order of their atomic numbers known as periods.
 
• Vertically the elements having identical chemical properties are clubbed together known as groups.
 
• The 18 groups are also known as columns and the 7 periods are also known as the rows.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d16a8368d409900ed90309e3e688edcd632301cf42a7b2027cd2c23c0712d711.png] 

Explanation:__

Periods:

__
 
• Elements are arranged in increasing atomic number of the elements in a period.
 
• One extra electron gets added to the outermost shell as we move along the periods from left to right.
 
• The electron gets added to the same shell or orbit and thus the electrons present for bonding increase by one unit.
 
• Thus, the shell number remains the same but the number of electrons present for bonding increases along a period.

Groups:

 
• Elements having the same number of outer electrons are put in the same group of the periodic table.
 
• When we move down a group, one extra shell gets added to the elements.
 
• The outermost shell has electrons present for bonding.
 
• Though the number of shells increases as we go down in a group, yet the number of electrons in the outermost shell remains the same.
 
• For example, the Halogens F, Cl, Br, I, At all belong to group 17 and have 7 electrons in the outermost shell.
 
• Similarly, Group 16 elements have 6 electrons in the outermost shell, group 15 has 5 electrons in the outermost shell, and so on.

• **Periodic table:-**
 
 
• It is a tabular presentation of the chemical elements, organized on the basis of their properties.
 
• Mendeleev’s Periodic Table (1869):
 
 
• It is based upon Mendeleev’s periodic law, which states, “Properties of the elements are the periodic function of their atomic masses.”
 
• Mendeleev is known as the father of the periodic table.
 
 
 
• Modern Periodic Law
 
 
• The physical and chemical properties of the elements are the periodic function of their atomic numbers.
 
 
 
• Modern Periodic Table:
 
 
• It is a graphical representation of the Aufbau principle.
 
• It is based on the electronic configuration of elements and contains 118 elements.
 
• There are 7 periods and 18 groups.
 
• Modern periodic table is classified as:
 
 
• i. s-block;

• iii. d-block;

• It is a chemical element with the symbol O and atomic number 8.
 
• It is a member of the chalcogen group in the periodic table, a highly reactive nonmetal, and an oxidizing agent that readily forms oxides with most elements as well as with other compounds. 
 
 
 
• Fermium:-
 
 
• Fermium is an actinide series radioactive metal with the atomic number 100.
 
• Fermium does not occur naturally and was discovered in the debris of the first hydrogen bomb explosion in 1953.

questions.question: Which element of the boron family has a high boiling point, making it ideal for recording temperatures that would vaporise a thermometer?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gallium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Gallium (Ga)** is a member of the boron family, positioned in **Group 13 of the Periodic Table**, with an **atomic number of 31 **and a relative **atomic mass of 69.723**.
 
• Gallium possesses a notably high boiling point of around** 2200°C **(3992°F), rendering it suitable for applications requiring the measurement of extreme temperatures that would vaporize conventional thermometers.
 
• Gallium finds various applications:
 
 
• **Specialized Thermometers: **Gallium is utilized in specialized thermometers engineered for high temperatures. These gallium thermometers provide a safe and accurate alternative to traditional mercury thermometers, which pose hazards due to mercury toxicity.
 
• **Semiconductor Production:** Gallium is a crucial constituent in semiconductor manufacturing. Gallium arsenide (GaAs) is employed to fabricate high-frequency electronic devices like microwave transistors and light-emitting diodes (LEDs).
 
• **Alloying Agent: **Gallium is alloyed with other metals to produce materials with specific properties. For instance, gallium-indium-tin alloys are utilized in liquid metal cooling systems for electronics, offering efficient heat transfer capabilities.
 
• **Nuclear Medicine:** Gallium-67, a radioactive isotope of gallium, plays a vital role in nuclear medicine for diagnostic imaging purposes. It is utilized to detect and diagnose certain diseases, aiding in medical diagnostics and treatment planning.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thallium **belongs to the boron family, specifically Group 13, in the periodic table, with an atomic number of 81. Due to its relatively low boiling point, thallium is not suitable for measuring high temperatures that would cause a thermometer to vaporize.
 
• **Aluminium** is another member of the boron family, with an atomic number of 13. While aluminium has a moderate boiling point, it is not exceptionally high, making it unsuitable for recording extremely high temperatures.
 
• **Indium** is also part of the boron family, with an atomic number of 49. Compared to gallium, indium has a lower boiling point, rendering it less suitable for applications requiring the measurement of high temperatures.
